title: Chemistry · Paper 2 (HL) — original full-format practice
subject: chemistry
instructions: Answer every question using the response area attached to it. An approved calculator is required. Use the original reference data supplied within this sample; no external data booklet is needed. Show calculations, units, diagrams and reasoning where required. No separate answer sheet is used.

resources.label: Original kinetics data
resources.text:
For reaction X + Y → products at constant temperature:
Experiment 1: [X] 0.10, [Y] 0.10, rate 2.0 × 10⁻⁴
Experiment 2: [X] 0.20, [Y] 0.10, rate 8.0 × 10⁻⁴
Experiment 3: [X] 0.20, [Y] 0.30, rate 2.4 × 10⁻³
Concentrations are mol dm⁻³; rates are mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

resources.label: Reference data for this sample
resources.text:
Relative atomic masses: H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00, Na 22.99, Mg 24.31, Cl 35.45
Specific heat capacity of water: 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹
Faraday constant: 9.65 × 10⁴ C mol⁻¹

questions.label: Question 1 — rate expression
questions.prompt: Determine the order with respect to X and Y, write the rate expression, and calculate the rate constant with units.

questions.label: Question 2 — equilibrium
questions.prompt: For an exothermic reversible reaction at equilibrium, explain the separate effects of increasing temperature and adding a catalyst on the equilibrium yield and the time to reach equilibrium.

questions.label: Question 3 — organic chemistry
questions.prompt: Propose a two-step synthetic route from ethene to ethanoic acid. Give reagents, conditions and displayed or structural formulas for the organic intermediates.

questions.label: Question 4 — spectroscopy
questions.prompt: A compound has molecular formula C₃H₆O₂. Explain how infrared and proton NMR evidence could distinguish methyl ethanoate from propanoic acid.

questions.label: Question 5 — stoichiometry and gases
questions.prompt: A volatile liquid has mass 0.742 g and occupies 286 cm³ as a gas at 99.0 kPa and 373 K. Determine its molar mass, propose a molecular formula from a supplied empirical ratio, and evaluate one source of systematic error.

questions.label: Question 6 — energetics
questions.prompt: Construct a Hess cycle to determine an unknown enthalpy of formation from combustion data. Then calculate the energy released by 12.0 g of the substance and state why the experimental value may be less exothermic.

questions.label: Question 7 — acids and bases
questions.prompt: Calculate the pH of a weak monoprotic acid and of the buffer formed after partial neutralization. Explain the response of the buffer to a small addition of strong acid.

questions.label: Question 8 — electrochemistry
questions.prompt: Use standard electrode potentials to predict the feasibility and direction of a redox reaction, write the overall equation, calculate E°cell and determine ΔG° at 298 K.

questions.label: Question 9 — structure and bonding
questions.prompt: Compare the bonding, structure and resulting physical properties of sodium chloride, graphite, silicon dioxide and iodine. Include conductivity in solid and liquid states where applicable.

questions.label: Question 10 — organic mechanisms
questions.prompt: For a route from propene to propanone, give reagents and conditions, classify each step, outline one mechanism with curly-arrow descriptions, and identify diagnostic spectroscopic evidence.
